title: Jev project submission
scope: Public open-source projects that use TypeSafe Jev for concrete typed decisions, including SDKs and integrations. Compatible reimplementations of the Jev API or decision schema are also in scope. Generic type-safe programming libraries are outside this scope.

categories.sdk: SDKs and clients whose primary purpose is calling the TypeSafe API
categories.integration: Adapters connecting Jev to an existing framework or platform
categories.developer_tools: Developer tools, code review, GitHub Actions, and coding-agent tools
categories.search: Search, retrieval, relevance ranking, and evidence selection
categories.applications: End-user applications using Jev decisions outside the other categories
categories.games: Games, robotics, and simulation with Jev selecting bounded actions
categories.research: Reproducible evaluations, benchmarks, and compatible reimplementations of the Jev decision layer
categories.other: No supported category, outside the directory scope, or insufficient evidence

checks.title: Concrete Jev integration
checks.question: Do the supplied source files show a concrete TypeSafe Jev API integration, provider integration, SDK implementation, or a compatible implementation of the Jev API or decision schema (for example serving the /v1/systemone contract) that is central to the repository's purpose? A README claim alone does not establish an implementation.
checks.yes: Source contains a TypeSafe API call, Jev provider call, implemented TypeSafe SDK methods used for a concrete purpose, or a compatible implementation of the Jev API or decision schema
checks.no: Only generic type safety, marketing claims, copied descriptions, or no source evidence of Jev integration or a compatible implementation

checks.title: Description supported by evidence
checks.question: Are the material claims in submission.description supported by the supplied README, source files, and repository facts (file existence such as action.yml, license, top-level paths, and package dependency names)? If there is no submission, judge the repository description. Do not treat an unsupported speed, accuracy, production-readiness, or safety claim as established.
checks.yes: The description gives a concrete purpose and its material claims match the supplied implementation or observed repository facts
checks.no: The description is misleading, unrelated, promotional without evidence, or claims functionality the files and repository facts do not show

checks.title: Usable setup documentation
checks.question: Does the supplied documentation explain how someone can install, configure, or run the project, including required provider credentials when applicable?
checks.yes: A reader has concrete setup instructions and knows which credentials or services are required
checks.no: Empty template, no usable instructions, or essential setup requirements are absent
